title: Hardik Pandya Named in India A Squad for Australia A Home Series in Puducherry
excerpt: The all-rounder, who has not played competitive cricket since IPL 2026, has been included in the one-day squad subject to fitness clearance as India plan his return ahead of the ODI World Cup.
body:
• Hardik Pandya has been named in India A's one-day squad for the home series against Australia A in Puducherry, subject to fitness clearance.
  • The all-rounder has not played competitive cricket since IPL 2026, spending months rehabbing at BCCI's Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru.
  • Devdutt Padikkal will captain the multi-day squad while Ruturaj Gaikwad leads the one-day side across five matches starting September 22.
  • Pandya's return is considered crucial to India's ODI World Cup preparations for the tournament in October-November 2027.

Hardik Pandya is set for a long-awaited return to competitive cricket after the BCCI named him in India A's one-day squad for the upcoming home series against Australia A in Puducherry. The 33-year-old all-rounder's inclusion, announced on Wednesday, is subject to fitness clearance.

Pandya has been out of action since the Indian Premier League 2026 season and has spent the intervening months recovering from a series of injuries at the BCCI's Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru. Back spasms during the IPL were followed by a leg strain while training ahead of the ODI series against Afghanistan in June, forcing him to miss that assignment entirely.

A Carefully Managed Comeback

The all-rounder has not played ODI cricket since the Champions Trophy final in March 2025, having rested from the 50-over format in the build-up to the T20 World Cup earlier in 2026. His inclusion in the India A squad suggests the selectors are looking to ease him back into match conditions rather than pushing for an immediate return to the senior side.

"India will hope Hardik clears his fitness assessment ahead of the Australia A series, and begins the process of slotting back into 50-overs rhythm."

— ESPNcricinfo

India's ODI World Cup campaign in October-November 2027 in Southern Africa looms as the primary motivation behind this measured approach. Pandya remains India's most accomplished seam-bowling all-rounder and is seen as central to their tournament plans, particularly in conditions that reward pace-bowling depth.

Padikkal and Gaikwad to Lead

The Men's Selection Committee named separate squads for the two formats. Devdutt Padikkal, fresh off a Player of the Series performance in India's 1-0 Test series victory over Sri Lanka where he scored 328 runs batting at number three, will captain the multi-day side. Sai Sudharsan, who missed the Sri Lanka series with a right toe injury, has been named vice-captain.

Ruturaj Gaikwad takes charge of the one-day squad, with Padikkal stepping into the vice-captain's role. The white-ball group includes several established domestic names: Rajat Patidar, Priyansh Arya, and emerging talent Naman Dhir, who recently struck a record 173 off 64 deliveries in the Sher-e-Punjab T20 League.

Series Schedule

The multi-day matches are scheduled for September 22–25 and September 29 to October 2, while the three one-day games will follow on October 6, 9, and 11. All five fixtures will be held in Puducherry, running concurrently with the senior team's five-match T20I series against the West Indies at home.

Fast bowler V Vyshak, named in the multi-day squad, is the only other player whose participation depends on fitness clearance. The squads otherwise feature a blend of proven performers like Shams Mulani, Tanush Kotian, and Tushar Deshpande alongside younger players staking their claim for international recognition.

What's Next

If Pandya passes the fitness assessment, the Australia A series will mark his first competitive outing in roughly five months. India's selectors will be watching closely to gauge not only his form with bat and ball but also whether his body can withstand the workload of multi-match assignments — a question that has defined his career since 2018.
